- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.3), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for risk reversal.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 1–2 days); apply smoothing filter to dampen overshoots.
- Forecast mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show upward trend, model often fails to revert; adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% per day after peak.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overpredict mid-term (days 10–20) when sentiment is volatile; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% in those periods.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misaligns with sentiment direction; align forecast slope with sentiment trend direction.
